title: From Research to Regulatory Infrastructure: A Deployment Framework for Auditable AI in Financial Regulation
content: A large number of AI models for financial regulation never reach actual application as they are designed as one-offs only, as inception prototypes. Instances of the lack of a collaboration tool that is scalable, auditable, and adheres to federal privacy laws are especially notable on the part of the U. S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), and financial institutions in the areas of anti-money laundering, securities monitoring and cross-border M&A due diligence. In this paper, we present a modular deployment framework to be used to translate auditable results of AI research into regulations. Application Programming Interface, which is the backbone of any finance institute or regulatory institution to connect with one another.First, the paper will define an API-based architecture that any financial institution or regulatory agency can integrate into—rather than having to build from scratch. Second, this paper correlates the framework with the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA), the Bank Secrecy Act, SEC Rule 17a-4 and the review requirements of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) to show how it can be embedded in current compliance workflows. Third, the paper presents a scenario-based estimate of potential operational benefits.A scenario-based analysis illustrates a potential 68% reduction in false-positive alerts under predefined assumptions, rather than an empirically established improvement across U.S. financial institutions Finally, this paper outlines a cross-agency, pilot initiative designed to share risk signals among the U. S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and banks, without sharing raw customer data. The paper also sketches a trajectory toward open-dource and standardization by considering auditable AI a public service, on par with a proprietary technology. This approach can speed the adoption of these systems by larger community banks and small compliance departments that don't have the resources to create them on their own. The platform facilitates existing regulatory initiatives to improve market integrity, anti-money laundering oversight and cross-border investment home monitoring.
